title: Personal Credit Cards: counting the balance owed from the card ledger for a closing autopay
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: balance owed counted from the ledger, for a closing autopay

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder closing a card that will still carry a balance records a closing fixed-amount autopay instruction, the fixed amount starts from the balance owed on the card at handling time, counted from the card's ledger as set out below.

## Rule

The balance owed is the total of the entries that raise what is owed, less the total of the entries that lower it, taking every such entry on the card's ledger at handling time. Because a fee reversal is among the entries that lower it, any fee already refunded as part of the closing is out of the balance owed.

| Entries that raise the balance owed | Entries that lower the balance owed |
|---|---|
| purchases | payments |
| cash advances | merchant credits |
| balance transfers | fee reversals |
| fees | interest reversals |
| interest charges | dispute credits |
| returned payments | rewards statement credits |
| dispute rebills | |

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger at handling time)

| Entry type | Total |
|---|---|
| purchases | 1850.00 USD |
| fees, including an annual fee of 80.00 USD | 112.00 USD |
| interest charges | 43.10 USD |
| payments | 600.00 USD |
| fee reversals, including the reversal of that annual fee posted today | 80.00 USD |

Balance owed: 1850.00 plus 112.00 plus 43.10 gives 2005.10; less 600.00 and 80.00 gives 1325.10 USD. The annual fee reversed today is out of the figure.

## Points of judgement

- A rewards redemption paid into a checking account moves no amount on the card's ledger among the entries listed, so it does not change this count; a rewards statement credit does lower it.
- A returned payment raises the balance owed, because it takes back the credit of the payment returned.
- The count uses the ledger entries themselves at handling time, so an entry posted earlier in the same handling is included.
